newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan to promote coffee in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan to promote coffee in Asia.

text.p: A group of coffee growers and exporters were to leave Friday on a visit to Korea and Japan to boost interest in Guatemalan coffee, said the president of National Coffee Association (Anacafe) Thursday.
"We don't have much (coffee) trade with Korea. We want to widen this developing market, we have never presented them our best coffees," Anacafe president Julio Arrivillaga told Reuters.
Arrivillaga said Anacafe had begun a promotion campaign for buyers last year in Northern Europe and the Asian trip was the next stage of the campaign.

The Guatemalan coffee delegation will make a presentation, including samples and tasting, to importers, traders and toasters in Seoul, South Korea, on Jan 28 and a similar presentation Jan 30 in Tokyo, he added.

Japan buys eight percent of Guatemalan coffee exports. Arrivillaga said the mission would promote high-quality coffee from five Guatemalan regions: Antigua, Atitlan, Huehuetenango, Coban and Fraijanes.
According to Arrivillaga, Guatemala is the fourth largest origin of coffee to Japan but sells little coffee to Korea.
The director of Anacafe's marketing commission and the president of the Coffee Exporters Association will travel with Arrivillaga to Asia.
Arrivillagas said Anacafe also has appointments to meet privately with different importers and toasters in Japan.
Following visits to Korea and Japan, the Anacafe representatives will attend the a meeting of the International Coffee Organization executive board, Feb 3-5 in Bali, Indonesia.
